blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Processing long videos with Vision-Language Models (VLMs) is bottlenecked by
the quadratic cost of visual tokens, making long-form inference prohibitively
expensive.
While single-axis compression methods mitigate this, they hit a hard efficiency
floor because they treat spatial and temporal redundancy independently.
We present VETO (Video Efficient Token Optimization), a training-optional plug-in
that eliminates this bottleneck through dual-axis compression: (i) an intra-frame compressor that merges semantically similar tokens within
each frame via optimal-transport inspired matching, and (ii) an inter-frame compressor that identifies and merges temporally redundant
frames.
The key design insight is hierarchical ordering: by first compressing spatial
dimensions, VETO drastically reduces the cost of subsequent global temporal
matching—bypassing the efficiency wall of single-axis approaches, with an
advantage that grows with modern fully-fused attention infrastructure.
Empirically, VETO achieves up to 45% faster inference (e.g., on
LLaVA-OneVision-7B) while preserving or improving accuracy.
Under extreme token starvation (10% budget), VETO outperforms VFlowOpt [ 32 ] (54.9%), VisionZip [ 31 ] (52.6%), and FastV [ 3 ] (47.9%) with 55.7% accuracy.
We demonstrate universal applicability across LLaVA-OneVision, InternVL-2.5,
and LongVA, with zero-shot accuracy preserved or improved in all cases.

Existing solutions trade off accessibility and performance.
Training-based methods require substantial compute.

We introduce VETO (Video Efficient Token Optimization), a training-optional plug-in that
resolves this through a dual-axis strategy.

blocks.en:
A critical property of VETO’s design is that its advantage over single-axis
baselines is hardware-agnostic —and in fact grows on modern,
optimized attention infrastructure.
Fully-fused attention kernels effectively absorb per-frame spatial reductions
from intra-only methods, but cannot absorb VETO’s total-sequence-length
reduction.
This means VETO’s relative speedup margin over single-axis baselines increases
on modern deployments, making it an increasingly compelling choice as inference
stacks continue to be optimized.

blocks.en:
System contribution. Beyond the algorithmic design, VETO is immediately deployable as a drop-in
module requiring no custom CUDA kernels or architectural modifications.
It operates as a pure tensor transformation—applied between the visual encoder
and the LLM—and is fully compatible with standard attention implementations
including FlashAttention.
The end-to-end latency measurements reported in this paper (visual encoder +
token compression + LLM inference) constitute a realistic systems-level
evaluation of deployment cost.

We validate VETO across three VLM families: LLaVA-OneVision [ 12 ] (0.5B and 7B), InternVL-2.5 [ 5 ] (1B), and

In the fully supervised setting (Section 4.3 ), VETO
additionally achieves state-of-the-art on long-form narrative benchmarks and competitive procedural action recognition.

blocks.en:
VETO is a training-optional plug-in that addresses the computational
bottleneck in video understanding through dual-axis compression: spatial

blocks.en: 3.1 Motivation: The Complexity Bottleneck
blocks.zh: 3.1 动机: 复杂博特伦克

blocks.en:
Standard VLM attention scales as 𝒪 ⁡ ( ( T ⋅ N ) 2 ) \mathcal{O}((T\cdot N)^{2}) .
Single-axis temporal methods reduce T T but must first compute a global
similarity matrix across fully uncompressed spatial tokens, introducing
a strict hardware-level latency floor that prevents optimal speed-ups.
VETO bypasses this floor through hierarchical ordering.
Intra-frame spatial compression first reduces the spatial dimension to N / k N/k at a cost of only 𝒪 ⁡ ( N 2 / k ) \mathcal{O}(N^{2}/k) per frame.
The subsequent inter-frame temporal compression then operates on this shrunken
feature space, requiring only 𝒪 ⁡ ( T 2 ⋅ C ) \mathcal{O}(T^{2}\cdot C) for global similarity
assessment (typically C ≪ N C\ll N ).
The effective attention complexity becomes 𝒪 ⁡ ( T ⋅ N 2 / k + T 2 ⋅ C ) \mathcal{O}(T\cdot N^{2}/k+T^{2}\cdot C) —fundamentally breaking the
single-axis latency floor.

Rationale for uniform partitioning. The modulo- k k partition is spatially uniform by design : every spatial
region contributes exactly one anchor, guaranteeing complete spatial coverage.
Content-adaptive anchor selection concentrates anchors in salient regions,
leaving peripheral areas without valid destinations—leading to precisely the
spatial collapse one might expect from aggressive compression.
In VETO, content-adaptiveness is reserved for the merging step
(Eq. 5 ): each source token is matched to its cosine-nearest
anchor, achieving semantic grouping.
Adding content-adaptive anchor scoring would require an additional 𝒪 ⁡ ( N 2 ) \mathcal{O}(N^{2}) pass, negating the efficiency gain.
Empirically, Table 4 confirms accuracy is stable across k ∈ { 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 } k\in\{2,3,4,5\} ; significant spatial collapse would manifest as
monotonic degradation, which is not observed.

Positional information. VETO operates on feature vectors already output by the frozen ViT encoder,
which has baked absolute positional information into each token prior to

The downstream LLM receives compressed tokens as a flat visual prefix with no

blocks.en: 5 Discussion
blocks.zh: 5 讨论情况

blocks.en:
A recurring theme across our ablations is a fundamental asymmetry between the
two compression axes.
Spatial (intra-frame) compression is highly robust: accuracy on VideoMME
remains within 0.6% across k ∈ { 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 } k\in\{2,3,4,5\} , corresponding to retaining
between 20% and 50% of per-frame tokens.
Temporal (inter-frame) compression is considerably more sensitive: degradation
becomes substantial below G ratio = 0.25 G_{\text{ratio}}=0.25 , and moderate at 0.50.
This asymmetry is not accidental—it reflects a structural property of video.
Individual frames encode highly redundant spatial information (textures,
backgrounds, repeated patterns), whereas temporal transitions encode causally
important events and state changes that are critical for reasoning tasks.
VETO’s design exploits this asymmetry by applying aggressive spatial
compression first and conservative temporal compression second, leading to
the recommended defaults k = 2 k=2 , G ratio ≥ 0.75 G_{\text{ratio}}\geq 0.75 .

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We present VETO, a training-optional dual-axis token compression plug-in for
video VLMs.
As a plug-in, VETO yields consistent latency reductions across model scales
(0.85–0.86 × \times on LLaVA-OneVision-7B; 0.55 × \times on
LLaVA-OneVision-0.5B; 0.86–0.90 × \times on LongVA-7B).
Its advantage over single-axis baselines grows on modern optimized attention
infrastructure, confirming the hardware-agnostic nature of the dual-axis
design principle.
Under extreme token starvation (10% budget), VETO establishes a new
state-of-the-art, outperforming all single-axis methods by a significant
margin.
In the fully supervised setting (Section 4.3 ), VETO
additionally achieves competitive procedural recognition (Breakfast:
94.4%, COIN: 92.7%).

By reducing token counts by up to 50% spatially and 25% temporally, VETO
directly reduces FLOPs and energy consumption during inference, contributing
to the goal of sustainable VLM deployment on consumer-grade hardware.

blocks.en:
All plug-in experiments are conducted on models up to 7B parameters.
At larger scales, attention patterns, token redundancy profiles, and hardware
bottlenecks may differ; empirical validation beyond 7B is left to future work.
Additionally, the intra-frame compressor inherits no text-query signal:
compression is purely content-based, not query-aware.

blocks.en:
The structural explanation: a frame’s N N tokens encode a static scene
where neighboring patches are often semantically redundant (uniform
backgrounds, repeated textures).
The uniform modulo- k k partition guarantees every spatial region
contributes one anchor, so merging 50–80% of tokens is safe.

结构解释:一个帧的N符号编码了静态场景
相邻的补丁常常是杂乱无章的(统一)
背景,重复的纹理).
统一的modulo- k k 分区保证每个空间区域
贡献一个锚,所以50-80%的地物合并是安全的。

blocks.en:
Temporal frames, by contrast, encode a causal sequence of events.
Each discarded frame may contain a unique transition or action state
that cannot be inferred from neighbors.
This is why degradation becomes non-linear below G ratio = 0.50 G_{\text{ratio}}=0.50 :
the model begins discarding irreplaceable causal information.

相形之下,时间框架编码了事件的因果序列.
每个被丢弃的框架可能包含一个独特的过渡或动作状态
这不能从邻居那里推断出来
因此,G比下降解为非线性:0.50G_{\text{ratio}}=0.50:
